question.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $x.$ First, we cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+1}{3} & =\frac{y-x}{2} \\ 2\cdot (2x+1) & =3\cdot (y-x) \\ 4x+2 & =3y-3x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we subtract $2$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x+2 & =3y-3x \\ 4x+2-2 & =3y-3x-2 \\ 4x & =3y-3x-2\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we add $3x$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & =3y-3x-2 \\ 4x+3x & =3y-3x-2+3x \\ 7x & =3y-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by $7:$

$$
\begin{aligned}7x & =3y-2 \\ \frac{7x}{7} & =\frac{3y-2}{7} \\ \frac{\cancel{7}x}{\cancel{7}} & =\frac{3y-2}{7} \\ x & =\frac{3y-2}{7}\end{aligned}
$$
